=== FIRST ===
Lecture: Lesson 2.2.1: Equations of Motion in Rectangular, Normal-Tangential, and Polar Coordinates

Section 1: Kinetics in Rectangular Coordinates (\\(\sum F_x = m a_x, \sum F_y = m a_y, \sum F_z = m a_z\\))
- Section Identity: Section 1: Kinetics in Rectangular Coordinates (\\(\sum F_x = m a_x, \sum F_y = m a_y, \sum F_z = m a_z\\))
- Core Understanding: When a particle moves in a 2D or 3D curved trajectory described by rectangular coordinates \\((x, y, z)\\), Newton's second law resolves into three independent scalar equations of motion: \\(\sum F_x = m a_x = m \ddot{x}\\), \\(\sum F_y = m a_y = m \ddot{y}\\), and \\(\sum F_z = m a_z = m \ddot{z}\\). This framework is especially useful when forces are expressed in terms of Cartesian components or when tracking independent 2D/3D component motions like robotic arms or aircraft maneuvers.
- Visual-First Explanation: A spatial 3D Cartesian coordinate frame tracking a particle moving along a 3D space curve. Three orthogonal force vectors (\\(F_x, F_y, F_z\\)) act on the particle, creating three proportional acceleration vectors (\\(a_x, a_y, a_z\\)) along each respective axis.
- Visual Scene Script: A particle of mass \\(m\\) moves along a spatial trajectory in a 3D Cartesian system \\((x, y, z)\\). Resultant force vector \\(\vec{F}\\) resolves into orthogonal components \\(F_x, F_y,\\) and \\(F_z\\) along the coordinate axes. Corresponding acceleration components \\(a_x = \ddot{x}, a_y = \ddot{y},\\) and \\(a_z = \ddot{z}\\) scale proportionally with mass \\(m\\). On the Kinetic Diagram side, the resultant inertial vector \\(m\vec{a}\\) resolves into \\(m a_x \hat{i} + m a_y \hat{j} + m a_z \hat{k}\\).
- Dynamic View Blueprint: Interactive 3D Cartesian view controls with force component sliders (\\(F_x, F_y, F_z\\)) showing live acceleration component outputs (\\(a_x, a_y, a_z\\)) and trajectory curve modification.
- Visual Learning Outcome: Students resolve force and acceleration vectors into independent Cartesian components (\\(\sum F_x = m a_x, \sum F_y = m a_y, \sum F_z = m a_z\\)) for curvilinear motion.
- Concept Check: How many scalar equations of motion are used for a particle moving in a 2D plane using rectangular coordinates? (Answer: Two equations: \\(\sum F_x = m a_x\\) and \\(\sum F_y = m a_y\\)).
- Conceptual Summary: In rectangular coordinates, kinetics resolves into \\(\sum F_x = m a_x, \sum F_y = m a_y,\\) and \\(\sum F_z = m a_z\\).
- شرح للجزء بالعامية المصرية: لما الجسم يتحرك في مسار منحني 2D أو 3D ونستخدم الإحداثيات الكارتيزية \\((x, y, z)\\)، بنفك قانون نيوتن الثاني لثلاث معادلات مستقلة: \\(\sum F_x = m a_x\\) و \\(\sum F_y = m a_y\\) و \\(\sum F_z = m a_z\\). كل اتجاه بيتحسب لوحده تماماً بدون ما يتدخل في الاتجاهات الثانية.
- القوانين (إن وُجدت): \\(\sum F_x = m a_x = m \ddot{x}, \quad \sum F_y = m a_y = m \ddot{y}, \quad \sum F_z = m a_z = m \ddot{z}\\)
- إسقاط على مثال أو موقف من الحياة اليومية لتثبيت الفهم: طائرة مقاتلة بتمشي في الفراغ، القوة المحركة من الموتور والرفع والجاذبية بيتفكوا لـ 3 مركبات على المحاور x, y, z وكل مركبة بتسبب تسارع موازي ليها في اتجاهها.

Section 2: Kinetics in Normal and Tangential Coordinates (\\(\sum F_t = m a_t, \sum F_n = m a_n, \sum F_b = 0\\))
- Section Identity: Section 2: Kinetics in Normal and Tangential Coordinates (\\(\sum F_t = m a_t, \sum F_n = m a_n, \sum F_b = 0\\))
- Core Understanding: When a particle moves along a known curved path, resolving forces into normal-tangential \\((n-t-b)\\) coordinates provides direct physical insight:
  1. Tangential Equation \\(\sum F_t = m a_t = m \frac{dv}{dt} = m v \frac{dv}{ds}\\): The sum of forces tangent to the path equals mass times tangential acceleration, governing changes in speed magnitude.
  2. Normal Equation \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\): The sum of forces acting inward toward the center of curvature equals mass times normal (centripetal) acceleration, governing changes in motion direction.
  3. Binormal Equation \\(\sum F_b = 0\\): Since motion is confined to the osculating plane, there is no acceleration along the binormal axis \\(b\\).
- Visual-First Explanation: A vehicle taking a banked curved turn. The moving \\((n, t, b)\\) coordinate frame shows tangential force \\(\sum F_t\\) accelerating the vehicle forward, normal force \\(\sum F_n\\) pulling inward toward the center of curvature with magnitude \\(m v^2/\rho\\), and binormal force balancing gravity and vertical reaction along the \\(b\\)-axis.
- Visual Scene Script: A car navigates a banked circular track. Moving axes \\((t, n, b)\\) attach to the car. Along the tangential axis \\(t\\), traction minus air resistance yields net force \\(\sum F_t = m a_t\\). Along the normal axis \\(n\\) pointing toward center \\(O'\\), horizontal normal force component plus static friction provides centripetal force \\(\sum F_n = m v^2/\rho\\). Along the binormal axis \\(b\\) (vertical to motion plane), forces balance (\\(\sum F_b = 0\\)). Increasing vehicle speed \\(v\\) causes required normal force \\(\sum F_n\\) to increase quadratically.
- Dynamic View Blueprint: Interactive banked turn simulator with speed slider \\(v\\), banking angle \\(\theta\\), and turn radius \\(\rho\\), displaying live vector balances for \\(\sum F_t\\), \\(\sum F_n = m v^2/\rho\\), and \\(\sum F_b = 0\\).
- Visual Learning Outcome: Students write kinetic equations along path coordinates (\\(\sum F_t = m a_t, \sum F_n = m v^2/\rho, \sum F_b = 0\\)) and understand centripetal force requirements on curved paths.
- Concept Check: What force provides the normal acceleration \\(m a_n = m v^2/\rho\\) when a car rounds an unbanked flat turn? (Answer: Static friction force \\(F_s\\) between the tires and the road surface directed inward toward the center of curvature).
- Conceptual Summary: In \\(n-t\\) coordinates, \\(\sum F_t = m a_t\\) governs speed changes, \\(\sum F_n = m v^2/\rho\\) provides centripetal turning force toward center \\(O'\\), and \\(\sum F_b = 0\\) maintains plane motion.
- شرح للجزء بالعامية المصرية: في نظام المماس والعمودي \\((n-t-b)\\)، المعادلات بيبقى ليها معنى فيزيائي واضح جداً:
  1) \\(\sum F_t = m a_t = m \frac{dv}{dt}\\): محصلة القوى المماسية هي اللي بتزود أو تنقص مقدار السرعة.
  2) \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\): محصلة القوى العمودية الموجهة لمركز التقعر هي القوة الجاذبة المركزية اللي بتجبر الجسم يلف في المنحنى.
  3) \\(\sum F_b = 0\\): المحور العمودي على مستوى الحركة ملوش أي عجلة لأن الحركة محصورة في مستوى المنحنى.
- القوانين (إن وُجدت): \\(\sum F_t = m a_t = m \dot{v}, \quad \sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}, \quad \sum F_b = 0\\)
- إسقاط على مثال أو موقف من الحياة اليومية لتثبيت الفهم: المطب الصناعي المائل في لفة الطريق السريع (Banked curve)، ميل السطح بيدي جزء من رد الفعل في الاتجاه العمودي لجوة (\\(\sum F_n\\)) عشان يساعد العربية تلف بأمان من غير ما تعتمد بالكامل على احتكاك الكاوتش.

Section 3: Kinetics in Polar Coordinates (\\(\sum F_r = m a_r, \sum F_\theta = m a_\theta\\))
- Section Identity: Section 3: Kinetics in Polar Coordinates (\\(\sum F_r = m a_r, \sum F_\theta = m a_\theta\\))
- Core Understanding: For particles tracked from a fixed origin \\(O\\) using radial distance \\(r\\) and angle \\(\theta\\), Newton's second law in polar coordinates decouples into radial and transverse force equations:
  1. Radial Equation \\(\sum F_r = m a_r = m (\ddot{r} - r \dot{\theta}^2)\\): Equates radial forces to mass times radial acceleration (combining radial linear acceleration \\(\ddot{r}\\) and centripetal term \\(-r \dot{\theta}^2\\)).
  2. Transverse Equation \\(\sum F_\theta = m a_\theta = m (r \ddot{\theta} + 2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\): Equates transverse forces to mass times transverse acceleration (combining angular acceleration \\(r \ddot{\theta}\\) and Coriolis term \\(2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta}\\)).
This framework is essential for analyzing slotted mechanical arms, rotating guides, and orbital satellite dynamics.
- Visual-First Explanation: A collar sliding along a rotating slotted arm. Force \\(F_r\\) acts along the arm length, while normal contact force \\(F_\theta\\) acts perpendicular to the slot wall. The arm's rotation generates centripetal and Coriolis inertial responses that balance the contact forces.
- Visual Scene Script: A collar of mass \\(m\\) slides along a smooth arm rotating at angular speed \\(\dot{\theta}\\) and angular acceleration \\(\ddot{\theta}\\). Radial force \\(\sum F_r\\) acts along unit vector \\(\hat{u}_r\\), driving radial motion \\(\sum F_r = m (\ddot{r} - r \dot{\theta}^2)\\). Transverse contact force \\(\sum F_\theta\\) exerted by the slotted guide wall acts along unit vector \\(\hat{u}_\theta\\), driving \\(\sum F_\theta = m (r \ddot{\theta} + 2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\). The Coriolis force component \\(m(2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\) highlights as a side-wall reaction force on the collar.
- Dynamic View Blueprint: Interactive rotating slotted guide simulation with sliders for \\(\dot{\theta}, \ddot{\theta}, r, \dot{r}\\), showing live vector balances for \\(\sum F_r\\) and \\(\sum F_\theta\\) and side-wall normal force.
- Visual Learning Outcome: Students apply kinetic equations in polar coordinates (\\(\sum F_r = m a_r, \sum F_\theta = m a_\theta\\)) to evaluate contact forces and accelerations in rotating mechanisms.
- Concept Check: If a collar slides outward at constant radial speed \\(\dot{r}\\) along an arm rotating at constant angular velocity \\(\dot{\theta}\\), is the transverse force \\(\sum F_\theta\\) zero? (Answer: No, because the Coriolis acceleration term \\(2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta}\\) is non-zero, requiring a transverse force \\(\sum F_\theta = m (2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\)).
- Conceptual Summary: Polar kinetics applies \\(\sum F_r = m (\ddot{r} - r \dot{\theta}^2)\\) and \\(\sum F_\theta = m (r \ddot{\theta} + 2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\) to determine radial forces and transverse guide contact forces.
- شرح للجزء بالعامية المصرية: في الإحداثيات القطبية (Polar coordinates)، معادلات نيوتن للفرعين الشعاعي والعرضي بتكون:
  1) \\(\sum F_r = m a_r = m (\ddot{r} - r \dot{\theta}^2)\\): محصلة القوى القطرية بتساوي الكتلة في (التسارع الشعاعي - العجلة الجاذبة نحو المركز).
  2) \\(\sum F_\theta = m a_\theta = m (r \ddot{\theta} + 2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\): محصلة القوى العرضية بتساوي الكتلة في (التسارع الزاوي + عجلة كوريوليس).
النظام ده ممتاز لحساب القوى على الأذرع الميكانيكية الدوارة والحلقات المنزلقة.
- القوانين (إن وُجدت): \\(\sum F_r = m a_r = m (\ddot{r} - r \dot{\theta}^2), \quad \sum F_\theta = m a_\theta = m (r \ddot{\theta} + 2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\)
- إسقاط على مثال أو موقف من الحياة اليومية لتثبيت الفهم: ذراع الروبوت الصناعي الدوار لما يتمدد لبرة بسرعة وهو بيلف، المحرك العرضي بيبذل قوة زيادة (\\(\sum F_\theta\\)) عشان يتغلب على قوة كوريوليس الناتجة عن تمدد الذراع أثناء الدوران!

  2) \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\): محصلة القوى العمودية الموجهة لمركز التقعر هي القوة الجاذبة المركزية اللي بتجبر الجسم يلف في المنحنى.
  3) \\(\sum F_b = 0\\): المحور العمودي على مستوى الحركة ملوش أي عجلة لأن الحركة محصورة في مستوى المنحنى.
- القوانين (إن وُجدت): \\(\sum F_t = m a_t = m \dot{v}, \quad \sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}, \quad \sum F_b = 0\\)
- إسقاط على مثال أو موقف من الحياة اليومية لتثبيت الفهم: المطب الصناعي المائل في لفة الطريق السريع (Banked curve)، ميل السطح بيدي جزء من رد الفعل في الاتجاه العمودي لجوة (\\(\sum F_n\\)) عشان يساعد العربية تلف بأمان من غير ما تعتمد بالكامل على احتكاك الكاوتش.

Section 3: Kinetics in Polar Coordinates (\\(\sum F_r = m a_r, \sum F_\theta = m a_\theta\\))
- Section Identity: Section 3: Kinetics in Polar Coordinates (\\(\sum F_r = m a_r, \sum F_\theta = m a_\theta\\))
- Core Understanding: For particles tracked from a fixed origin \\(O\\) using radial distance \\(r\\) and angle \\(\theta\\), Newton's second law in polar coordinates decouples into radial and transverse force equations:
  1. Radial Equation \\(\sum F_r = m a_r = m (\ddot{r} - r \dot{\theta}^2)\\): Equates radial forces to mass times radial acceleration (combining radial linear acceleration \\(\ddot{r}\\) and centripetal term \\(-r \dot{\theta}^2\\)).
  2. Transverse Equation \\(\sum F_\theta = m a_\theta = m (r \ddot{\theta} + 2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\): Equates transverse forces to mass times transverse acceleration (combining angular acceleration \\(r \ddot{\theta}\\) and Coriolis term \\(2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta}\\)).
This framework is essential for analyzing slotted mechanical arms, rotating guides, and orbital satellite dynamics.
- Visual-First Explanation: A collar sliding along a rotating slotted arm. Force \\(F_r\\) acts along the arm length, while normal contact force \\(F_\theta\\) acts perpendicular to the slot wall. The arm's rotation generates centripetal and Coriolis inertial responses that balance the contact forces.
- Visual Scene Script: A collar of mass \\(m\\) slides along a smooth arm rotating at angular speed \\(\dot{\theta}\\) and angular acceleration \\(\ddot{\theta}\\). Radial force \\(\sum F_r\\) acts along unit vector \\(\hat{u}_r\\), driving radial motion \\(\sum F_r = m (\ddot{r} - r \dot{\theta}^2)\\). Transverse contact force \\(\sum F_\theta\\) exerted by the slotted guide wall acts along unit vector \\(\hat{u}_\theta\\), driving \\(\sum F_\theta = m (r \ddot{\theta} + 2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\). The Coriolis force component \\(m(2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\) highlights as a side-wall reaction force on the collar.
- Dynamic View Blueprint: Interactive rotating slotted guide simulation with sliders for \\(\dot{\theta}, \ddot{\theta}, r, \dot{r}\\), showing live vector balances for \\(\sum F_r\\) and \\(\sum F_\theta\\) and side-wall normal force.
- Visual Learning Outcome: Students apply kinetic equations in polar coordinates (\\(\sum F_r = m a_r, \sum F_\theta = m a_\theta\\)) to evaluate contact forces and accelerations in rotating mechanisms.
- Concept Check: If a collar slides outward at constant radial speed \\(\dot{r}\\) along an arm rotating at constant angular velocity \\(\dot{\theta}\\), is the transverse force \\(\sum F_\theta\\) zero? (Answer: No, because the Coriolis acceleration term \\(2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta}\\) is non-zero, requiring a transverse force \\(\sum F_\theta = m (2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\)).
- Conceptual Summary: Polar kinetics applies \\(\sum F_r = m (\ddot{r} - r \dot{\theta}^2)\\) and \\(\sum F_\theta = m (r \ddot{\theta} + 2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\) to determine radial forces and transverse guide contact forces.
- شرح للجزء بالعامية المصرية: في الإحداثيات القطبية (Polar coordinates)، معادلات نيوتن للفرعين الشعاعي والعرضي بتكون:
  1) \\(\sum F_r = m a_r = m (\ddot{r} - r \dot{\theta}^2)\\): محصلة القوى القطرية بتساوي الكتلة في (التسارع الشعاعي - العجلة الجاذبة نحو المركز).
  2) \\(\sum F_\theta = m a_\theta = m (r \ddot{\theta} + 2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\): محصلة القوى العرضية بتساوي الكتلة في (التسارع الزاوي + عجلة كوريوليس).
النظام ده ممتاز لحساب القوى على الأذرع الميكانيكية الدوارة والحلقات المنزلقة.
- القوانين (إن وُجدت): \\(\sum F_r = m a_r = m (\ddot{r} - r \dot{\theta}^2), \quad \sum F_\theta = m a_\theta = m (r \ddot{\theta} + 2 \dot{r} \dot{\theta})\\)
- إسقاط على مثال أو موقف من الحياة اليومية لتثبيت الفهم: ذراع الروبوت الصناعي الدوار لما يتمدد لبرة بسرعة وهو بيلف، المحرك العرضي بيبذل قوة زيادة (\\(\sum F_\theta\\)) عشان يتغلب على قوة كوريوليس الناتجة عن تمدد الذراع أثناء الدوران!
